deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the preceding folio. It records a damping experiment on an oscillating magnet (magnetometer), of the kind Gauss and Weber ran in Göttingen in the 1830s on magneto-electric induction. Runs alternate between 'Kette offen' (circuit open) and 'Kette geschlossen' (circuit closed). The aim is to compare the damping of the magnet's oscillations in the two states; the extra damping when the circuit is closed comes from induced currents.

Columns, for oscillation number n (97–100, 107–110, 113–116, 123–126):
- clock time, given only at the first of each group of four (11h18'27", 25'31", 29'46", 37'0");
- a reading a_n near 994–982, whose role is not explained on the page (perhaps a position or rest-point reading; unsure);
- the amplitude (arc) A_n in scale divisions;
- log10 A_n to five decimals. Verified: e.g. log10 508.45 = 2.706248 and log10 377.3 = 2.576687.

Step 1 (the braces). For each group of four, Gauss takes the arithmetic mean of the four logarithms. He writes it with an extra half-digit, e.g. '2.70314.5' means 2.703145.
- n = 97–100 (open): (2.70625+2.70420+2.70217+2.69996)/4 = 2.703145. This belongs to the mean epoch n = 98.5.
- n = 107–110 (open): 10.72828/4 = 2.682070, at n = 108.5.
- n = 113–116 (closed): 10.64253/4 = 2.6606325, at n = 114.5.
- n = 123–126 (closed): 10.35169/4 = 2.5879225, at n = 124.5.

Step 2 (the margin numbers). Two groups of the same circuit state are separated by 10 oscillations. The logarithmic decrement per oscillation is therefore λ = (mean log of earlier group − mean log of later group)/10. Gauss records 10^5·λ, assigned to the midpoint epoch.
- Open: (2.703145 − 2.682070)/10 = 0.0021075, written 210.75 at n = 103½.
- Closed: (2.6606325 − 2.5879225)/10 = 0.0072710, written 727.10 at n = 119½.

Step 3 (Recapitulation). The decrements from this and the previous page are listed at midpoints every 16 oscillations. Open circuit: 7½: 192.85; 39½: 192.58; 71½: 197.15; 103½: 210.75. Closed circuit: 23½: 724.125; 55½: 722.70; 87½: 741.02; 119½: 727.10. All are 10^5 × common-log decrement per oscillation.

The point of the recapitulation (my interpretation): the closed-circuit decrement is about 3.7 times the open-circuit one. The difference, roughly 0.0053 per oscillation in log10 (natural-log decrement about 0.0122), is the damping due to the induced current. That is the quantity needed in the Gauss–Weber theory of induction damping. The open-circuit damping is attributed to air resistance and similar causes.

Side remark (mine): the timings give about 42.4 s per 10 oscillations for 97→107 (424 s/10) and about 43.4 s for 113→123 (434 s/10). This is a long-period instrument. The difference is far too large to be the damping effect on the period: (λ_e/π)^2 ≈ 3·10^-5.
errors: log10(501.15) = 2.699968, so 2.69997 to five places; Gauss writes 2.69996 (last-digit slip of 1 unit).
log10(484.25) = 2.685070, so 2.68507; Gauss writes 2.68506 (last-digit slip of 1 unit).

The effect of these slips on the group means is only 0.25e-5 each. On the recorded open decrement 210.75 (in units of 1e-5 per oscillation) the net effect is 0.000. The 101.15 slip lowers the first mean and the 484.25 slip lowers the second mean by the same amount, so the decrement is unchanged (strictly 210.75 either way).
All four means and both decrements are arithmetically correct given the written logarithms.

results.what: Logarithmic decrement of a damped magnetometer oscillation, obtained from means of log-amplitudes of two groups of oscillations 10 swings apart
results.modern_name: logarithmic decrement of damped oscillations (method of grouped means)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber (Göttingen Magnetic Union, 1830s); the logarithmic decrement concept is standard in their magnetometer work

results.what: Comparison of damping with circuit open vs closed, isolating the damping due to induced currents (ratio about 3.7)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and W. Weber (1830s); Weber's published work on the damper and induction

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine laboratory reduction from the Gauss–Weber induction experiments: log-amplitude means and logarithmic decrements with the circuit open and closed. The method and the physics are well known as theirs.

transcription_corrections: Mean values like '2.70314.5' denote 2.703145 (extra half-digit), not a separate number; likewise 2.66063.25 = 2.6606325.
Margin '210.75' belongs between the two open-circuit groups (epoch 103½), and '727.10' between the two closed-circuit groups (epoch 119½).
In row 114 the first reading 984.35 has an overwritten digit ('98(4/7).35'); 984.35 is consistent with neighbours.
In the Recapitulation, '87½' is written over another number (possibly 81/87); 87½ is correct by the 16-step sequence.
